title: Secure Role-Based Authentication
desc: The application features a secure architecture that uses HTTPOnly cookies for JWT management, effectively blocking XSS attacks. Strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) ensures Students, Teachers, and Admins dynamically receive the correct frontend views and remain securely restricted from unauthorized Flask API routes.
img_caption: Teacher Assignments UI showcasing role-based access control in action
p1: Keeps JWTs locked safely away from malicious JavaScript
p2: Protects backend endpoints with custom Flask decorators
p3: Uses industry-standard password hashing and route validation

title: Relational Database Design
desc: Built with a flexible database foundation, the system uses SQLite for fast out-of-the-box development and PostgreSQL for rock-solid production. Powered by the SQLAlchemy ORM, the schema seamlessly handles deeply nested relationships linking students, group assignments, multi-row rubrics, and the actual reviews.
p1: Efficiently queries and manages complex many-to-many linkages
p2: Uses Marshmallow schemas to serialize database objects into clean JSON
p3: Leverages declarative mapping to elegantly structure the database tables

title: React & TypeScript Frontend
desc: The frontend is powered by React 18 and Vite, delivering an incredibly fast and responsive user experience. Strict TypeScript interfaces catch bugs long before runtime, while React Context handles global state management to seamlessly power accessibility features like dark mode.
img_caption: Clean UI toggled in Dark Mode
p1: Leverages Vite for optimized builds and instant HMR
p2: TypeScript types are aligned perfectly with the backend schemas
p3: React Context manages app-wide global state and accessibility features

title: Docker & GitHub Actions Setup
desc: Designed with a container-first approach, the application runs exactly the same way locally as it does in production. Networked Docker containers isolate the UI, API, and database, while a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline automatically runs tests on every push to ensure maximum code reliability.
p1: Maintains separate networked containers for the UI, API, and Database
p2: GitHub Actions automatically triggers pytest to catch regressions on push
p3: Easily deployable to cloud platforms thanks to a stateless API design
